text:
ConocoPhillips fell 6.1% today, wiping out most of its gains from yesterday's rally. The drop follows news that Saudi Arabia's damaged pipeline will restart in days, easing concerns about oil supply disruptions—and oil prices fell sharply on that news. The company also faces headwinds from the dramatic gap between U.S. crude ($107) and world crude ($131), a widening spread that typically pressures U.S. oil producers' margins and suggests global demand concerns are outweighing supply relief.

The broader context is mixed for energy companies right now. While diesel prices hitting all-time highs ($6.31/gallon) normally benefit refiners and producers, the geopolitical volatility in the Middle East and the UK's inflation jump underscore persistent economic uncertainty. Continental Resources' move into Venezuela development suggests some operators see opportunity in new regions, but ConocoPhillips' pullback today reflects the market reassessing energy stocks once immediate supply fears eased.
